chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Waleed reported to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt who said: I heard al-Ridha, Ali ibn Musa, peace be upon them both, supplicating with words, so I memorized them from him. And whenever I invoked them during hardship, Allah relieved me. They are:

"O Allah, You are my Trust in every distress, and You are my Hope in every hardship; and in all that befalls me, You are my Trust and my Shelter. How many a distress weakens the heart, and the remedy diminishes, and the affairs become helpless, and the near one and the distant one and the friend abandon, and the enemy gloats — I brought it before You, and complained of it to You, inclined to You regarding it beside all others, and You dispelled it, removed it, and sufficed me in it. So You are the Provider of every bounty, and the Source of every need, and the Final Refuge of every desire.

So for You is abundant praise, and to You belongs plentiful favour. With Your blessings, all righteousness is fulfilled. O One known for His Grace, gracious, and O One who is described with Grace — bestow upon me from Your Grace a grace that would suffice me from the grace of all others besides You, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful ones."

key_terms.ثقة: thiqa (trust): complete reliance and confidence in Allah
key_terms.دعاء: du'a (supplication): personal prayer of invocation to Allah
key_terms.فرج: faraj (relief): deliverance from hardship, a key Shia eschatological concept
key_terms.كرب: karb (distress): deep grief or anguish that overwhelms the heart
key_terms.معروف: ma'ruf (grace/goodness): divine favor and generosity; a recurring keyword in this du'a

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication of Imam al-Ridha for times of distress and hardship?
ai.summary: Al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, a trusted companion of Imam al-Ridha (the eighth Imam, d. 203 AH), reports memorizing this personal supplication directly from the Imam during a private audience. The du'a expresses complete reliance on Allah during tribulation, acknowledging that when all human support fails — whether from family, friends, or distant acquaintances — only Allah relieves distress. Imam al-Ridha's circle would have understood this prayer in the context of the political pressures the Imam faced under the Abbasid caliphate, making the theme of divine reliance especially poignant. The supplication concludes with a theologically rich play on the word 'ma'ruf' (grace/goodness), asking Allah — who is known for His grace and described by it — to bestow a grace sufficient to free the supplicant from dependence on anyone else.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 4. He said: Abul Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Waleed reported to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ja’ffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Swalt who said: I heard al-Ridha ‘Ali ibn Musa invoking a prayer, so I memorized it from him. And whenever I invoked it during hardship, Allah relieved me. It is:

"O Allah! You are my Trust in every distress, and You are my Hope in every hardship; And in all that befalls me, You are my Trust and my Shelter; How much of grief that weakens the heart, and has but little way of escape, and when the affairs lack any remedy, When the near ones and the distant ones, and the friends let me down, and the enemies taunt, I came unto You and complained to You, inclined to You beside all others, And You dispelled the grief and relieved the affliction, and became Sufficient for me, So You are the Provider of all bounties, and the Source for all needs, and the Final Refuge for every desire.

So, for You is abundant praise, and to You belongs the plentiful favour. With Your blessings, all righteousness is fulfilled. O One who is known for His Grace, and the One praised for His Grace, bless me with the Grace which would enable me to dispense with kindness from others, I beseech Your mercy, O Most Merciful."
